Source   Edit  

Bounded Balance tree (weight-balanced tree) implementation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weight-balanced_tree

References:

  • Adams, "Implementing Sets Efficiently in a Functional Language", CSTR 92-10
  • Straka, "Adams' Trees Revisited", 2011

func `<`[K, U, V](s1: BBTree[K, U]; s2: BBTree[K, V]): bool {.inline.}

Alias for isProperSubset(s1, s2). Returns true if the keys in s1 form a strict or proper subset of the keys in s2.

A strict or proper subset s1 has all of its keys in s2 but s2 has more elements than s1.

Source   Edit   
func `<=`[K, U, V](s1: BBTree[K, U]; s2: BBTree[K, V]): bool {.inline.}

Alias for isSubset(s1, s2). Returns true if s1 is subset of s2.

A subset s1 has all of its members in ts2 and s2 doesn't necessarily have more members than s1. That is, s1 can be equal to s2.

Source   Edit   
func `=?=`[K, U, V](s1: BBTree[K, U]; s2: BBTree[K, V]): bool {.inline.}
Alias for setEqual(s1, s2). Returns true if both s1 and s2 have the same keys and set size. Source   Edit   
func add[K, V](root: var BBTree[K, V]; key: K; value: V)
Mutable wrapper: inserts (key, value) pair into root. Source   Edit   
func contains[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; key: K): bool
Returns true if the key is in the tree root otherwise false. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func countKeys[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]): int
Used for unit testing only; normally use len to get the number of keys. Source   Edit   
func del[K, V](root: var BBTree[K, V]; key: K)
Mutable wrapper: removes key from root. Source   Edit   
func delMax[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]): BBTree[K, V]
Delete the maximum element from tree root. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func delMin[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]): BBTree[K, V]
Delete the minimum element from tree root. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func difference[K, V](tree1, tree2: BBTree[K, V]): BBTree[K, V]
Returns the asymmetric set difference between tree1 and tree2. In other words, returns the keys that are in tree1, but not in tree2. O(M + N) Source   Edit   
func disjoint[K, V](tree1, tree2: BBTree[K, V]): bool
Returns true iff tree1 and tree2 have no keys in common. O(N) where N is len(tree1) Source   Edit   
func find[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; key: K; default: V): V
Retrieves the value for key in the tree root iff key is in the tree. Otherwise, default is returned. O(log N) Source   Edit   
proc fold[K, V, T](root: BBTree[K, V]; f: proc (key: K; val: V; base: T): T;
                   base: T): T
Applies the proc f to each value of tree root in reverse order (right to left). Uses the base value for the first rightmost operand. Source   Edit   
func getMax[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; default: (K, V)): (K, V)
Retrieves the key,value pair with the largest key in the tree root For an empty tree default is returned. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func getMin[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; default: (K, V)): (K, V)
Retrieves the key,value pair with the smallest key in the tree root For an empty tree default is returned. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func getNext[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; key: K; default: (K, V)): (K, V)
Returns the key,value pair with smallest key > key. It is almost inorder successor, but it also works when key is not present. If there is no such successor key in the tree, default is returned. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func getNth[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; index: int; default: (K, V)): (K, V)
Get the key,value pair of the 0-based index key in the tree root when index is positive and less than the tree length. Or get the tree length plus index key in the tree root when the index is negative and greater than the negative tree length. Otherwise, default is returned. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func getPrev[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; key: K; default: (K, V)): (K, V)
Returns the key,value pair with largest key < key. It is almost inorder predecessor, but it also works when key is not present. If there is no such predecessor key in the tree, default is returned. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func insert[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; key: K; value: V): BBTree[K, V]
Returns a new tree with the (key, value) pair added, or replaced if key is already in the tree root. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func intersection[K, V](tree1, tree2: BBTree[K, V]): BBTree[K, V]
Returns the set intersection of tree1 and tree2. In other words, returns the keys that are in both trees. When viewed as maps, returns the key,value pairs for keys that appear in both trees; the value each key is selected from tree1, so this function is asymmetrical for maps. If you need more control over how the values are selected for duplicate keys, see uintersectionMerge. O(M + N) Source   Edit   
func intersectionMerge[K, V](tree1, tree2: BBTree[K, V];
                             merge: proc (k: K; v1, v2: V): V {.noSideEffect.}): BBTree[
    K, V]
Returns the set intersection of tree1 and tree2. In other words, returns the keys that are in both trees. When viewed as maps, returns the key,value pairs for keys that appear in both trees; the value for each key is the result of the supplied merge function, which is passed the common key, and the values from tree1 and tree2 respectively. O(M + N) Source   Edit   
func isBalanced[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]): bool
Used for unit testing only; returns true if the tree is balanced, which should always be the case. Source   Edit   
func isProperSubset[K, U, V](tree1: BBTree[K, U]; tree2: BBTree[K, V]): bool
Returns true iff the keys in tree1 form a proper subset of the keys in tree2. In other words, if all the keys that are in tree1 are also in tree2, but there are keys in tree2 that are not in tree1. O(N) where N is len(tree1) Source   Edit   
func isSubset[K, U, V](tree1: BBTree[K, U]; tree2: BBTree[K, V]): bool
Returns true iff the keys in tree1 form a subset of the keys in tree2. In other words, if all the keys that are in tree1 are also in tree2. O(N) where N is len(tree1) Use isProperSubset instead to determins that there are keys in tree2 that are not in tree1. Source   Edit   
func len[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]): int
Returns the number of keys in tree at root. O(1) Source   Edit   
func map[K, V, T](root: BBTree[K, V];
                  f: proc (key: K; val: V): T {.noSideEffect.}): BBTree[K, T]
Returns a new tree with the keys of tree root and values that are the result of applying f to each key and corresponding value. So, for example, to construct a tree with values replaced by concatenated string of key,value pairs, you could use
map(root, proc (k: int, v: int): string = $k & ":" & $v)
Source   Edit   
func rank[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; key: K; default: int): int
Retrieves the 0-based index of key in the tree root iff key is in the tree. Otherwise, default is returned. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func remove[K, V](root: BBTree[K, V]; key: K): BBTree[K, V]
Removes key from tree root. Does nothing if the key does not exist. O(log N) Source   Edit   
func setEqual[K, U, V](tree1: BBTree[K, U]; tree2: BBTree[K, V]): bool
Returns true if both tree1 and tree2 have the same keys. Source   Edit   
func symmetricDifference[K, V](tree1, tree2: BBTree[K, V]): BBTree[K, V]
Returns the symmetric set difference between tree1 and tree2. In other words, returns the keys that are in tree1, but not in tree2, union the keys that are in tree2 but not in tree1. O(M + N) Source   Edit   
func toSet[K](keys: openArray[K]): BBTree[K, bool]

Creates a BBTree set that contains the given keys with value true.

Example:

var numbers : BBTree[int,bool] = toSet([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
assert numbers.contains(2)
assert numbers.contains(4)
Source   Edit   
func union[K, V](tree1, tree2: BBTree[K, V]): BBTree[K, V]
Returns the union of the sets represented by the keys in tree1 and tree2. When viewed as maps, returns the key,value pairs that appear in either tree; if a key appears in both trees, the value for that key is selected from tree1, so this function is asymmetrical for maps. If you need more control over how the values are selected for duplicate keys, see unionMerge. O(M + N) but if the minimum key of one tree is greater than the maximum key of the other tree then O(log M) where M is the size of the larger tree. Source   Edit   
func unionMerge[K, V](tree1, tree2: BBTree[K, V];
                      merge: proc (k: K; v1, v2: V): V {.noSideEffect.}): BBTree[
    K, V]
Returns the union of the sets represented by the keys in tree1 and tree2. When viewed as maps, returns the key,value pairs that appear in either tree; if a key appears in both trees, the value for that key is the result of the supplied merge function, which is passed the common key, and the values from tree1 and tree2 respectively. O(M + N) but if the minimum key of one tree is greater than the maximum key of the other tree then O(log M) where M is the size of the larger tree. Source   Edit
